newsitem.title: SINGAPORE: PECC seeks Asian financial market reform.
newsitem.headline: PECC seeks Asian financial market reform.

text.p: The Pacific Economic Cooperation Council (PECC) issued a report on Saturday proposing improvements to the Asia-Pacific region's financial markets.

The PECC think-tank said in a report released in Singapore that financial markets were an important ingredient of market-based economic growth and their smooth functioning would enhance regional cooperation and prosperity.

The report entitled 'Financial Markets Development -- A Road to Pacific Economic Growth' will be presented on Saturday to Asia-Pacific Economic Cooperation (APEC) finance ministers at their meeting in Cebu, in the Philippines.

It said that although economies in the Asia-Pacific region were enjoying strong development, they still faced many challenges, one of which was developing and promoting reform of financial and capital markets.
The PECC Financial Markets Development project group put forward recommendations on actions both the public and private sectors should take to improve financial markets in the region.
The proposals covered three broad areas, the first being the standardisation of requirements for disclosure of financial information.
The report said standardisation would facilitate listing on foreign stock exchanges and fund raising in both domestic and foreign markets.
"Clear disclosure of corporate information will improve transparency and enable investors to more effectively assess firms' operations and financial conditions," it said.
The PECC recommended a list of standardised disclosure requirements.

It also urged firms and stock exchanges in the region to adopt international standards being drawn up by the International Organisation of Security Commissions and the International Accounting Standards Committee.
The report said the private sector was gaining importance as a source of infrastructure financing.

"The source economies could further deregulate their capital markets to encourage the issuance of foreign securities; relax restrictions imposed on foreign securities holdings of institutional investors; promote infrastructure funds and develop private guarantee companies," the PECC said.
It also said further liberalisation of cross border capital flows should be encouraged as the benefits outweigh the costs.
It said it was desirable for economies in the region to establish cooperative macroeconomic-level frameworks for financial and exchange rate stabilisation.

The PECC is an independent, policy-oriented organisation of business, academic and government representatives from 22 Asia-Pacific economies. It is the only non- governmental body among APEC's three official observers.
